# Daily report: 2026-11-25 (SW-589)

## Done

**G9: default models (PR 3 branch `tram/sw-589-training-defaults`)**
- Applied Eran's answer: the default models are now chosen by run type (per cluster or per trace); both default to the notebook models.
- Each model file now records where its values came from. Eran's `xgboost_depth2_mds` added as an optional model.
- No run changes: every shipped config trains the same models, and all model hashes are unchanged. 17 tests.

**M6 / M7: GRID_CLEAN plateau median (PR 2 branch `tram/sw-589-preprocess-features`)**
- Applied Eran's answer: default median band widened to −60 / +120; `relive_beta` pinned at the old band so it reproduces past results.
- Clearer wording for what `plateau_median_global: false` means.
- The layout a run used is now saved as `grid_clean_layout.json` in the run folder.
- M7 option b (median from training patients only): won't fix.

**G11: blip filter (PR 2 branch)**
- Avichai decided: the blip filter is on by default. A trace is kept only with at most 4 repaired samples before the descent, 3 after, 9 in total; type_5 exempt.
- Rejected traces are marked invalid: they stay in the audit and the estimation set, not in training.
- The 7 experiment configs keep it off, so they reproduce past results.
- 16 tests.

**H5: one feature extractor (done on the Linux clone)**
- Avichai decided: keep only the TSF extractor. It is now the only one; the `use_tsf_features` switch is gone.
- Default `tsf_interval_counts: [1]` gives the same features as before under new names, so no result change.
- Q3 resolved: poolsel always gets TSF names.

**W7 group A: training, thresholds, tuning (PR 3 branch, 4 commits)**
- M1, H6, G6 fixed; Q4 answered; L15 partly fixed.
- Tuning now picks thresholds with the same code as training.
- Per-trace training is confirmed to fit on traces.
- Tuning trials that can't fit now fail instead of scoring 0, and resuming a study with a changed config is refused.
- 9 tests. No change to shipped models or default runs.

**Test failures and tickets**
- The old test failures are explained:
  - 2 were Windows-only test issues, now fixed;
  - 2 are real bugs, now ticketed: SW-610 (missing `scripts/protocol6_con_fact.py`, Avichai) and SW-611 (`control_group` ignored when `control_groups` is set, Tram).
- Suite on the PR 3 branch: 557 passed. The remaining failures are the known ones.
- Jira:
  - W6 (SW-599) and SW-603 are Done.
  - W4, W5 and W7 (SW-597, SW-598, SW-600) are In Progress.
  - SW-605 moved to W8 with SW-604.

## Blockers

**Eran**
- G9: confirm the model name (`balanced_random_forest_lucia_legacy` is `balanced_rf_aggregated_tuned_lucia_legacy`?) and that clustering off counts as per trace.
- M6: should the median use valid traces only, and what counts as valid?
- M7: file format of the saved layout, and the `layout_file` key.
- M6: a before/after median on real data.
- G10: which version of his preprocessing module is final.

**Avichai**
- G11: confirm our datasets have the `blip_tuple` column, and the note on the total limit (today's daily meeting).

**W5 group B (Eran answered 2026-11-25)**
- L14: both de-duplication methods built as an opt-in `bootstrap_scheme` (default `with_replacement`, byte-identical): `score_unique` and `rotating`. Default runs unchanged; 8 tests. Which one to adopt is the campaign comparison (with M4, M5). Only `recursive` having no ranking is left as is.
- G20: BLOCKED. Eran deferred the missing-value policy to Gilad and Avichai.

**Gilad, Avichai (new, from Eran's reply 2026-11-25)**
- G20 missing-value policy: pick one — report the rate and warn, drop a feature above a threshold, fill with training-pool medians then select and train on that table, or drop all-missing columns (zero is never a fill).
- M5 spin-off: should the same per-trace equal weighting also apply in training, not only selection? Wider than SW-589.

**Gilad, Eran, Avichai (W7 group B)**
- M12 and M13.
- L15: the Youden search and the xgboost version pin.

**Monday's defaults (SW-606)**
- G3 default values and Q1 (where the current defaults came from) are still open.

## Next steps
- Tram reviews W7 group A, then commit its findings text (uncommitted now).
- Review H5 on the Linux clone, then bring it into the PR 2 branch.
- G11 and the M6/M7 decisions are in the findings file and pushed (a10bd17). Update G11 if the dataset check finds a problem.
- Start W8 (reports, SW-601), including SW-604 and SW-605, while the blockers are open.
- Apply the answers above as they come in.

**Title:** SW-589 (PR 1/5): Review findings triage and safe fixes

**Branch:** `tram/sw-589-pr38-findings` into `master`
**Reviewers:** Gilad, Avichai

## What this PR does
Goes through the PR 38 review findings in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md` and lands the fixes that don't change model results. Every finding now has a Resolution line. No model numbers change.

## Findings closed in this PR
| Status | Findings |
|---|---|
| Fixed here (12) | G12, G18, G22, M11, L2, L3, L4, L5, L6, L12, L16, L19 |
| Already fixed on master, confirmed (6) | G1, G4, G5, G7, G13, L9 |
| Won't fix (3) | G2, L1, L13 |
| Waiting (2) | G3 (meeting on 2026-11-23, SW-606), G9 (Eran) |

Each fix has a test that fails on the old code. The other findings come in later PRs.

## Changes reviewers should know about
- Configs whose per-trace settings contradict each other are now rejected before the run starts (G22). All shipped configs still load.
- A holdout run without training now only extracts features and skips the whole-pool selection (G18). Holdout results are identical.
- The removal audit counts visits (G12) and records GRID_CLEAN drops (M11).
- New warnings when the threshold falls back to 0.5 (L5, L6) and when several models are trained (L4).
- Tuning modules import again (SW-603).

## Tests
- 473 passed (386 on master). The 3 failures and 1 collection error also fail on master.
- A system test runs holdout with and without whole-pool selection and checks that all 34 output tables match.

## Found during this work
- SW-603: tuning modules failed to import (fixed here).
- SW-604: model reports from a training run cover only the last model.
- SW-605: `--resume` always reruns the features stage.

## How to review
Start with the Resolution lines in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`. There is one commit per finding, so `git show <hash>` shows one fix and its test. The largest changes are in `src/core/stages/features.py` (G18) and `src/core/config/validate.py` (G22).

# Review: SW-589 W3, config contract and defaults

- **Status:** `[x]` approved by Tram on 2026-11-20 · **Jira:** SW-596 (Done)
- **Branch:** `tram/sw-589-pr38-findings`
- **Range:** `sw589-W3-start..sw589-W3-review` (5 commits)
- **Goal of W3:** a run's config is checked before it starts, and the defaults are chosen deliberately.
- **Closed early (Tram, 2026-11-19):** G3 and Q1 wait for the 2026-11-23 meeting and G9 waits for Eran, so W3 closes with G22 as its only fix. G3 gets its own commit after the meeting.

## Scope and new statuses

| Finding | Was | Now | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| G22 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Per-trace settings checked when the config loads |
| G9 (+ H2) | ACCEPTED | **WAITING (Eran)** | No per-trace models from Eran on any branch; questions recorded |
| G3 | ACCEPTED | **WAITING (Gilad, Avichai, SW-606)** | Defaults to decide at the 2026-11-23 daily meeting |
| Q1 | open | open, **→ SW-606** | Same meeting as G3 |

1 FIXED; 3 waiting on others, each with an owner.

## Commits

| Hash | Finding | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 66e81aa | G22 | Check the per-trace config keys when the config is loaded |
| 87446e0 | (all FIXED) | Show only the current state of fixed findings (Tram's rule). Docs only |
| bb69e45 | G9 | Mark as waiting for Eran's per-trace models. Docs only |
| 8fb1b35 | G22 | Explain why null stays true with clustering off. Docs only |
| 2a8ed48 | G3, Q1 | Mark as waiting for the defaults decision (SW-606). Docs only |

## Files changed (riskiest first)

1. **`src/core/config/validate.py`** (G22): new `per_trace_rows`, `resolve_allow_multi_trace`, `_validate_model_report_levels`; called from `validate_pipeline_config`. Replaces the one old check (`unit: trace` + `false`).
2. **`src/core/stages/training.py`** (G22): `training_settings_from_config` uses the shared resolver instead of its own copy of the rule.
3. **`src/core/holdout_estimation.py`** (G22): `prepare_rows` uses the resolver; it read `null` as false before.
4. **`src/core/stages/model_reports.py`** (G22): the missing trace-statistics error names the right setting.
5. **Docs:** `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md` (G22, G9, G3, Q1, and the FIXED-items rewrite).
6. **Tests:** 1 new file, 2 changed.

## Test evidence

**Test cases per finding (30 new cases, 2 changed):**

| Finding | Cases | Test file | What they cover | Red before the change? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G22 | 7 | `test_trace_mode_config.py::test_agreeing_keys_load_and_resolve_the_same_in_training` | every agreeing combination of unit × clustering × flag loads, and training resolves the same value | Pass both times: pins the behaviour that had to stay |
| G22 | 3 | `::test_disagreeing_multi_trace_is_rejected_at_load` | `true` on cluster rows, `false` on `unit: trace`, `false` with clustering off | 2 red (cluster + true, clustering off + false); `unit: trace` + false was already rejected |
| G22 | 4 | `::test_report_levels_that_cannot_be_built_are_rejected_at_load` | patient mixed with cluster; cluster with `source: training`; patient with `source: holdout`; trace on a cluster run | All 4 red (only failed at the report stage before) |
| G22 | 3 | `::test_report_levels_that_can_be_built_load` | auto + patient; holdout + cluster on a cluster run; holdout + trace/cluster on a trace run | Pass both times |
| G22 | 11 | `::test_every_shipped_config_still_loads` | all 11 YAMLs in `configs/pipeline/` and `experiments/` | Pass both times: no shipped config is affected |
| G22 | 1 | `::test_holdout_estimation_resolves_null_like_training` | holdout estimation gets `allow_multi_trace=True` for a per-trace run with `null` | Red (got False) |
| G22 | 1 | `::test_missing_trace_statistics_hint_names_the_real_gate` | the missing-file error mentions `allow_multi_trace` | Red |
| **Total** | **30** | | | **9 red before, all pass now** |

**Changed tests:**
- `test_training_stage.py::test_explicit_multi_trace_setting_overrides_clustering_mode` → `test_multi_trace_on_cluster_rows_is_rejected`. It asserted the mismatch G22 removes; it now expects the rejection (red before the change).
- `test_pipeline_runner.py::test_holdout_model_reports_depend_on_holdout_not_training`: asked for `trace` reports on a cluster run, which G22 rejects. It tests stage planning only, so its levels are now `["cluster"]`.

**Red check method:** `git stash` of `src/` only, run the new tests against the old code, then restore.

**Full suite:**

| | Passed | Failed | xfailed | Collection errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| After W2 | 443 | 3 | 6 | 1 |
| W3 review | **473** (+30) | 3 (same) | 6 (same) | 1 (same) |

- **Invariants:** 18 passed, 6 xfailed (SW-568). No XPASS.
- **System:** 10 passed; the 1 baseline failure (`test_unused_study_group_is_left_out[NOT_LC-L-RAD]`) is unchanged.
- **Synthetic run:** the system tests run the full pipeline through config loading, so every stage now passes the new check. No separate run needed: G22 changes validation only.

## Metric comparison
Not needed. G22 rejects configs that disagree and resolves `null` the same way training already did; every shipped config loads and resolves as before. No model numbers change.

## Decisions made
1. **Clustering off → `null` resolves to true** (confirmed by Tram, documented in G22, 8fb1b35). The finding proposed false; that would make holdout keep one channel per measurement.
2. **`source: auto` keeps its run-time check.** The `holdout` command picks the source only when it runs, so config loading can't know it.
3. **Holdout estimation fixed in G22.** Same rule; it read `null` as false.
4. **W3 closed early** (Tram): G3 and Q1 → SW-606, G9 → Eran.

## Follow-up Jira tickets created
- **SW-606:** decide the default config values (G3, Q1) at the 2026-11-23 daily meeting. Sub-task of SW-589, linked to SW-596.

## Questions for Tram
None open for W3. Waiting on others: G3/Q1 (meeting 2026-11-23), G9 (Eran).

## How to review
```bash
git log --oneline sw589-W3-start..sw589-W3-review
git diff --stat sw589-W3-start..sw589-W3-review
git diff sw589-W3-start..sw589-W3-review -- src/core/config/validate.py   # riskiest
git show 66e81aa                                                          # G22
```

# SW-589 — Work through the PR 38 review findings

## Context
SW-589 (assigned to you, due 2026-11-24, reporter Avichai Toubi) says: branch from current master, go through every field in "the PR 38 file", and for each one (1) validate its status, (2) fix it if needed, (3) record what changed. The task is done when every field is resolved and a PR with the updates is complete. The ticket also asks you to note ideas that would help the team work better in this repo.

"The PR 38 file" is `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`: Gilad's review of PR #38 (merge 649d87f). It has 63 findings, and each has a **Status** (ACCEPTED / WONTFIX / FIXED, or the ID of another finding) and a **Verified** value:
- **G1–G18**: Gilad's notes. 5 FIXED, 1 WONTFIX, 12 ACCEPTED. G6, G9 and G10 are waiting for Eran; G8, G11 and H5 are marked "avichai".
- **H1–H6**: High. H1–H4 point to G14, G9, G11 and G10.
- **M1–M19**: Medium, all ACCEPTED.
- **L1–L19**: Low, all ACCEPTED.
- **Questions for the author (1–5)**.

(`docs/PR38.pptx` is a separate how-to deck for `scripts/publish_clinical_dataset.py`. It is not the findings list.)

## Step-by-step process

### 0. Confirm scope (before coding)
Ask Avichai two things:
- Are G8, G11 and H5 ("avichai") and G6, G9 and G10 ("waiting for Eran") yours to do, or only yours to check status on?
- Is one PR acceptable, or should the work be split into several PRs?

Default if there's no answer: one branch, with one commit per finding (or per tightly related group). Owned and blocked items get their status checked only.

### 1. Branch
`git checkout master && git pull && git checkout -b tram/SW-589-pr38-findings`
Put the Jira key in the branch name so Bitbucket links the branch to SW-589.

### 2. Add a tracking column to the file
Use the file itself as the tracker, so there is a single source of truth. In each section table (G / H / M / L), add a **Resolution** column, and under each finding add a one-line `**Resolution:**` entry giving the commit hash, the files changed, the test added, or the reason no change was needed. Update the status vocabulary under "How to read this page": keep ACCEPTED / WONTFIX / FIXED and add **BLOCKED (owner)** for items waiting on someone else, **INVALID** (the claim is shown to be wrong) and **NOT REPRODUCED** (you couldn't trigger it, waiting for the reviewer to confirm).

### 3. Validation pass (read-only; covers all 63 items)
For every finding, open the `Where:` locations on current master and classify it:
- **FIXED items (G1, G4, G5, G7, G13)**: check the fix actually landed on master, since several notes say "uncommitted". Example: G4 means `configs/pipeline_v2/grid_clean_preprocessing.yaml` should be gone, but G11 still cites it. Note that G18 says the pipeline config dir is now `configs/pipeline/` and no longer `configs/pipeline_v2/`, so re-resolve every path first.
- **ACCEPTED items**: check the problem still exists on master (later merges such as #49 parallel holdouts and #50 plateau norm may have touched it). If it's already gone, mark it FIXED and cite the commit.
- **ACCEPTED but not verified in the repo**: reproduce before fixing. How depends on the Verified value:
  - `yes`: confirmed in code during the review. Re-read the code on current master and confirm it's unchanged.
  - `sub-review` / `sub-review (synthetic)` / `sub-review (real CSV)` (H6, M3–M13, M15–M19): the evidence was tests in `/tmp` that are no longer in the repo. Write a failing test in `tests/` that reproduces the problem through the real code path, then fix it.
  - `no` (G6, G8, G9, G10): G6 is itself a check (training happens on traces). Do it and report the result. G8, G9 and G10 are feature requests, so "verify" means confirming the gap still exists. They are also blocked on Eran or Avichai.
  - `—` (G15–G18): tasks, not bugs, and G15–G17 have no location. Agree the scope with the reporter before doing anything.
  - L1–L19: no Verified column. Treat them like `sub-review`.
  - Before deciding: make sure your attempt matches the conditions the finding describes (config flags such as `grid_clean` / `blip_filter` enabled, sensor types, data shape such as many traces per patient). A bug on a path that's off by default is still a bug.
  - Result (choose one):
    - **Reproduced**: set Verified to `yes (<test or file:line>)`, then fix it in step 4.
    - **Already fixed by a later commit**: set **FIXED** and cite the commit.
    - **INVALID**: you can show the claim is wrong (a code line that already handles the case, or a passing test of the exact scenario). Record the evidence. The finding itself is not valid.
    - **NOT REPRODUCED**: you tried and it didn't happen, but you can't rule it out. Record what you tried (config, data, test), leave the code unchanged, and ask Gilad to confirm before closing it.
  - Add INVALID and NOT REPRODUCED to "How to read this page", and list every item with these two statuses in the PR description for the reviewer.
- **Pointer items (H1–H4)**: they follow their target finding.
- **WONTFIX (G2)**: confirm with the reporter, then leave as is.

Output: the table filled in with a validated status. Commit this on its own ("Validate PR38 findings against master") so the reviewer sees the triage before the fixes.

### 4. Fix pass, in this order
1. **Small, clear-cut correctness bugs**: M19 (prevalence shadowing), M14 (RBC sign), M9 (search window), M8 (missing end-bound check), L9 (NaN trigger crash), L5/L6 (silent 0.5 threshold, at least add a warning), L12 (late fusion default), L19 (stale doc refs). Each gets a unit test in `tests/` that fails before the fix.
2. **Tracker and audit items you can do alone**: G12 (n_remaining_visits in `src/core/removal_audit.py`), G18 (git commit/branch on the tracker, and holdouts starting at feature selection), G14 (record holdout membership), M11 (log GRID_CLEAN drops to the tracker).
3. **Config cleanup**: G3 (redefine the `validation_only.yaml` defaults, at most 5 default YAMLs). Agree the values with Avichai or Gilad first, because this changes every run.
4. **Methodology / leakage items** (M1, H6, M2–M5, M12, M13, M15–M18): each one changes model numbers, so discuss before changing it. Some may become WONTFIX or a separate ticket.
5. **Blocked or owned items** (G6, G8, G9, G10, G11, H5, G15–G17): record the status and owner, and don't implement them unless step 0 assigns them to you.
6. **Questions for the author**: write down the answers you get, or mark them still open.

After each fix: update that finding's Status and Resolution line in the same commit (message `SW-589 <ID>: <summary>`).

### 5. Verify
- `pytest` (see `pytest.ini`) passes after every commit. Before you start, record the baseline count (the review notes 135/135 non-tuning tests passing).
- For fixes that change pipeline behavior (G12, G14, G18, M11), run one small pipeline run with `scripts/lucia_pipeline.py` on a small dataset and check the tracker/audit workbook shows the new fields.
- Before opening the PR, check that every row in the findings tables has a final Status and a Resolution.

### 6. Team-improvement notes
Keep a running list as you go, for example: findings tracked in a .md with no owner or ticket column; config paths that drift (`pipeline_v2` vs `pipeline`); "uncommitted" fixes recorded as FIXED; no stage test with grid_clean enabled. Put the list in the PR description or a Jira comment on SW-589.

### 7. PR and ticket
- Open a Bitbucket PR to master titled `SW-589: Resolve PR38 review findings`. In the description, give a summary table (fixed / validated already fixed / wontfix / blocked with owner / invalid / not reproduced), with the invalid and not-reproduced items highlighted for Gilad, and the team-improvement notes.
- Comment on SW-589 with the PR link and a list of the blocked items, then move the ticket to review/done once the PR is merged.

## Critical files
- `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`: the tracker
- `src/core/removal_audit.py`, `src/core/v2_pipeline_run.py`, `src/core/stages/{features,preprocessing,training,holdout}.py`, `src/core/pipeline_runner.py`, `src/core/train.py`, `src/visualization/feature_and_patient_score_report.py`, `model_report.py`, `trigger_detection.py`, `plateau_normalization.py`
- `configs/pipeline/validation_only.yaml`
- `tests/`

Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

Atlassian MCP server. Three layers of tools:
1. Primary tools (e.g. getJiraIssue, searchJiraIssuesUsingJql, searchConfluence, getConfluenceContent) are already in your tool list. Call them directly.
2. `discover` — when you do not know an operation's name, describe the goal. Returns `results` (each with the exact `name` + `inputs` + the matching execute-family tool for read/write/destructive operations). Do not discover an operation you already have as a primary tool.
3. Run a discovered operation with the execute-family tool matching its risk tier: `executeRead({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for read-only lookups, `executeWrite({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for non-destructive creates/updates, `executeDestructive({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for deletes/irreversible changes. Only call with an operation `name` from discover results or one already in your tool list; never guess, assume, or invent a name — when unsure, call discover first.

cloudId:
- If YOUR client session has no site context, call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE and reuse the returned cloudId. On any execute-family call, always pass cloudId as a TOP-LEVEL argument (sibling of `name`/`inputs`), never inside `inputs`.

Other context:
- The current user's accountId is available from `atlassianUserInfo`.
- Slim large responses with `responseFields` (dot paths) or a `view` preset (compact/evidence/full).

# Jira custom fields (story points, etc.)
Default view is compact — custom fields are omitted unless you pass view: evidence/full, or fields with this site's customfield_* IDs (IDs differ per site). Values appear under fields.customFields, not as top-level customfield_* keys.

# Recovery protocol
1. On a tool error, retry once with corrected input
2. On a missing operation, re-run `discover` with different keywords.

Confluence access links: For /wiki/access-link/ URLs, first call resolveConfluenceAccessLink with access_link set to the full URL. Use its returned content ID. Keep the same access_link on EVERY later supported call, including retries, pagination, and comment-type queries. Never probe without the link. Never use the token as an ID or this URL as content_url.

- When creating an HTML or text-based file, always ask the user whether they would like to upload it to Atlassian Artifacts. If they do, use `discover` to retrieve `createArtifactsUpload` (step 1) and `publishArtifact` (step 2).

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. <?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId

MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). After create_session, call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey — it is your primary tool; its output is a REFERENCE to adapt to the target project, not final code.

CODE-TO-DESIGN WORKFLOW (code → Figma):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.
2. Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session before any file tool; call create_new_file first if a new file is needed. Then ALWAYS call search_de… [truncated]

## claude.ai Google Drive
Drive can read the user's files, but it may refuse to move or trash a file that wasn't made through this connector, even one the user owns. Before you move a file with update_file, check the file's canMoveItemWithinDrive capability; before you trash a file with trash_file, check its canTrash capability. If the results you have don't show them, call get_file_metadata for that file first. Skip each file where the value is false, because Drive will refuse the change, and do the rest. If Drive refuses a file anyway, don't retry it, request access, or make a copy; carry on with the other files. At the end, tell the person which files you skipped or Drive refused, with a link to each, and that they can make those changes in Drive.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option. - Use the max or ultra level only when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask for one, never on your own judgment: they are the costliest reviews and start many reviewer subagents.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- ship-local (ship): Commit and push your work and open a pull request if the branch has none, review it in this session, fix the real problems, then watch the pull request (CI failures, conflicts, and review comments) until it is merged or closed, for up to 7 days. Claude is told never to merge the pull request. - Never call it yourself: only a line that the user types starts it. If they ask for it in other words, tell them to type /ship.
- steward: Watch the current branch's open pull request in this session and handle CI failures, conflicts, and review comments until it's merged or closed, for up to 7 days. It doesn't review the code first. Claude is told never to merge the pull request. - Never call it yourself: only a line that the user types starts it. If they ask for it in other words, tell them to type /steward.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- claude-approvals: Use BEFORE creating, changing, cleaning up or explaining a Claude Approvals policy file (.claude/approvals.yml) or custom classifier (.claude/classifiers/), or answering a question about its check, cost or speed. Edits that look harmless can let changes merge unreviewed. Also before or after anybody uninstalls or suspends the Claude GitHub App. Not for CODEOWNERS, branch protection, GitHub Actions or Claude Code's own permission settings.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

## claude.ai Atlassian MCP
Atlassian MCP server. Three layers of tools:
1. Primary tools (e.g. getJiraIssue, searchJiraIssuesUsingJql, searchConfluence, getConfluenceContent) are already in your tool list. Call them directly.
2. `discover` — when you do not know an operation's name, describe the goal. Returns `results` (each with the exact `name` + `inputs` + the matching execute-family tool for read/write/destructive operations). Do not discover an operation you already have as a primary tool.
3. Run a discovered operation with the execute-family tool matching its risk tier: `executeRead({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for read-only lookups, `executeWrite({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for non-destructive creates/updates, `executeDestructive({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for deletes/irreversible changes. Only call with an operation `name` from discover results or one already in your tool list; never guess, assume, or invent a name — when unsure, call discover first.

cloudId:
- If YOUR client session has no site context, call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE and reuse the returned cloudId. On any execute-family call, always pass cloudId as a TOP-LEVEL argument (sibling of `name`/`inputs`), never inside `inputs`.

Other context:
- The current user's accountId is available from `atlassianUserInfo`.
- Slim large responses with `responseFields` (dot paths) or a `view` preset (compact/evidence/full).

# Jira custom fields (story points, etc.)
Default view is compact — custom fields are omitted unless you pass view: evidence/full, or fields with this site's customfield_* IDs (IDs differ per site). Values appear under fields.customFields, not as top-level customfield_* keys.

# Recovery protocol
1. On a tool error, retry once with corrected input
2. On a missing operation, re-run `discover` with different keywords.

Confluence access links: For /wiki/access-link/ URLs, first call resolveConfluenceAccessLink with access_link set to the full URL. Use its returned content ID. Keep the same access_link on EVERY later supported call, including retries, pagination, and comment-type queries. Never probe without the link. Never use the token as an ID or this URL as content_url.

# Atlassian Artifacts
- When creating an HTML or text-based file, always ask the user whether they would like to upload it to Atlassian Artifacts. If they do, use `discover` to retrieve `createArtifactsUpload` (step 1) and `publishArtifact` (step 2).

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, open, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file
- figma.com/spec/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Specs file, load the figma-spec skill and use use_figma

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). After create_session, call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey — it is your primary tool; its output is a REFERENCE to adapt to the target project, not final code.

CODE-TO-DESIGN WORKFLOW (code → Figma):
1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.
2. Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session before any file tool; call create_new_file first if a new file is needed. Then ALWAYS call sea… [truncated]

## claude.ai Google Drive
Drive can read the user's files, but it may refuse to move or trash a file that wasn't made through this connector, even one the user owns. Before you move a file with update_file, check the file's canMoveItemWithinDrive capability; before you trash a file with trash_file, check its canTrash capability. If the results you have don't show them, call get_file_metadata for that file first. Skip each file where the value is false, because Drive will refuse the change, and do the rest. If Drive refuses a file anyway, don't retry it, request access, or make a copy; carry on with the other files. At the end, tell the person which files you skipped or Drive refused, with a link to each, and that they can make those changes in Drive.

## codegraph
# Codegraph — available (per-project; pass projectPath)

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of a codebase's symbols, edges, and
files (30+ languages): one `codegraph_explore` call returns the verbatim, line-numbered source
of the relevant symbols PLUS the call paths between them and a blast-radius
summary — replacing a grep + Read loop with one round-trip.

This server started somewhere with no `.codegraph/` of its own, so there is no
default project — but the tools are available and work **per project**:

- To query a project that HAS a `.codegraph/` index (e.g. a service inside a
  monorepo, or a second repo), pass its path as `projectPath` to
  `codegraph_explore` (and any other codegraph tool). Codegraph resolves the
  nearest `.codegraph/` at or above that path and answers from it — for as many
  projects as you like in one session.
- For a project with no `.codegraph/`, use your built-in tools (Read/Grep/Glob)
  for that project. Indexing is the user's decision — don't run it yourself, but
  if it comes up they can run `codegraph init` in a project to enable codegraph
  there (a new index is picked up live, no restart).


---
CodeGraph v1.6.4 is available (this server is running v1.6.2). Update with `codegraph upgrade`. This server keeps running the old version until the user upgrades — mention it when convenient; do not run the upgrade yourself.
